domain: forced displacement - corridor-level asylum-application surge prediction (international organisation publisher)
prediction_question: For an asylum corridor (country of origin O, country of asylum H) whose total government-procedure asylum applications in year D are at least 500 (persons, all application types summed), will that corridor's total government-procedure asylum applications in year D+1 be at least twice the year-D value? Annual grain, measured 2000-2025; a useful prediction enables humanitarian reception planning and resettlement budgeting ahead of the surge year rather than after it.
prediction_time: Annual publication-lag NOWCAST - the accepted abs-visitor-arrivals-direction pattern, and it must not be described as a future-event forecast. The prediction instant is the publication of year-D complete annual data on the machine-fetchable channel: UNHCR's annual statistical cycle lands mid-year in D+1 (Global Trends), and the HDX distribution of this dataset was observed refreshing on 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22 and 2026-08-20, with the 2026-08-20 resource carrying complete data through 2025. At that instant every feature is a corridor-year total for years <= D. The target year D+1 has PARTIALLY ELAPSED at the instant (the 2026-08-20 instant lies inside target year 2026, which started 2026-01-01) but its value is entirely UNPUBLISHED: on this channel no D+1 value exists until ~mid-D+2, and for most non-EU hosts no public monthly corridor data exists at all (Eurostat monthly data covers EU hosts only and is outside this channel's shipped features). So the claim recorded here is value-unavailability at the instant, not that the target window follows the instant. A strictly-future variant (at the same instant, predict year D+2 >= 2x the last PUBLISHED year D) was considered and rejected at discovery: the doubling baseline must be published at the instant, so a strict future window forces a two-year-back comparison, a different label and different measured base rates - a different task. The HDX archive is revised in place (current-vintage), so construction pins the fetched snapshot by sha256 and states values as construction-time vintage - the same documented posture as abs-visitor-arrivals-direction. Dated example in notes.md.
target_definition: Binary exceedance: label 1 iff the corridor-year (D+1, O, H) government-procedure persons total (sum of all application-type rows; a missing corridor row with the host still reporting counted as 0 applications) is >= 2 x the corridor-year (D, O, H) total. Label source: the same 'Number of Applications' column of the HDX CSV at year D+1; the year-D+1 value and everything derived from it are excluded from shipped features. Censoring: corridors whose host reports no G/P rows at all in D+1 (33 of 7,622 eligible rows, 0.43%) are excluded as unobserved targets, not counted as 0. Note what the target does NOT measure: temporary-protection registrations (e.g. Ukrainians in the EU from 2022) are not asylum applications and do not enter this stream.

split_strategy: Temporal split on corridor-year label windows (Government procedure, persons, sum of all application-type rows; eligibility: year-D corridor total >= 500 and host active in D+1). Candidate partition, counts computed from the source 2026-10-23: train label-years 2001-2016: n=3,677 rows, 302 positives (x2 prevalence 8.2%), 198 distinct (origin, label-year) positive clusters; eval label-years 2017-2021: n=1,918, 166 positives (8.7%), 109 clusters; holdout label-years 2022-2025: n=1,994, 234 positives (11.7%), 135 clusters. Both classes present in every label-year of every window (positives per label-year range 2-92). Surge origins differ across windows (train: SYR/AFG/IRQ; eval: VEN/AFG/COD; holdout: TUR/VEN/IND/AFG/CUB). Construction may adjust boundaries inside this measured envelope but must recompute and record counts on the frozen artifact; the prevalence drift (more surges later) is a property of the period, to document at construction.

measurements.panel_shape_measured_2026_10_23: Applications CSV: 120,597 data rows, 13 columns, years 2000-2025 (26), 215 origin codes, 130 asylum-country codes. Columns: Year, Country of Origin Code/Name, Country of Asylum Code/Name, Procedure Type/Name, Application Type Code/Name, Application Data Type/Data, Application Average Persons Per Case (all zero), Number of Applications (all integer). No month column. Provenance mix (skill requirement): Procedure G=105,862 / U=13,955 / J=780 rows; Data Type P=113,635 / C=6,962. The task is defined on the G/P stream only (99,281 rows, 6,936 distinct corridors, 33.7M applications); the UNHCR-procedure stream (13,640 persons rows) is a separate RSD population, not summed in, and the task does not cover corridors served only by UNHCR procedure.
measurements.duplicate_rows_resolved_2026_10_23: 20,851 of 73,051 G/P corridor-year cells (28.5%) carry multiple rows with the same (Year, Origin, Asylum, Procedure, ApplicationType, DataType) key but different counts (e.g. 2000 AFG->DEU G/V/P: 5,380 vs 5,756; 2000 AFG->AUS G/V/C: 90 vs 1,326). Identical rows in all other columns; present in every year incl. 2025 (35 groups), and identical in the per-country extracts (verified on asylum_applications_residing_deu.csv). Resolution rule: SUM all G/P rows per corridor-year. Basis: cross-checks against the primary national publisher's own published host-year totals (BAMF, which is UNHCR's source for Germany) match the sum-all rule to within 0.005-0.09% in four different years, while the max-rule matches BAMF's first-application figure - i.e. the duplicate rows are disjoint components (first vs follow-up applications) exported under one type code, so summing reconstructs the total. See bamf_cross_check_2026_10_23.
measurements.bamf_cross_check_2026_10_23: Sum-all G/P host-year totals vs BAMF's published totals (Erst- und Folgeantraege): DEU 2000: 117,600 vs 117,648 (-0.04%); DEU 2010: 48,544 vs 48,589 (-0.09%); DEU 2015: 476,630 vs 476,649 (-0.004%); DEU 2016: 745,510 vs 745,545 (-0.005%). The max-rule matches BAMF first applications for the same years (441,898 vs 441,899 in 2015), confirming the duplicates are first/follow-up pairs. BAMF figures from bamf.de Asylgeschaeftsstatistik / Bundesamt in Zahlen (searched and read 2026-10-23); UNHCR's Germany data is sourced from BAMF. This is the publisher-total cross-check for the panel construction rule.
measurements.label_family_measured_2026_10_23: On eligible corridor-years (G/P sum-all >= 500 at D, host active in D+1; n=7,589 across 2000-2024): decline (D+1 < D) 57.3%; growth >25% 27.4%; growth >50% 18.5%; >=2x 9.3%; >=3x 4.2%. Chosen label: >=2x (doubling), a ~9% prevalence exceedance target in the house family of the other published exceedance tasks. Alternatives measured and recorded; construction must not re-tune the threshold after seeing scores.
measurements.split_window_counts_2026_10_23: x2 label, computed from the source: train label-years 2001-2016 n=3,677 / 302 positives / 198 (origin, label-year) positive clusters; eval 2017-2021 n=1,918 / 166 / 109; holdout 2022-2025 n=1,994 / 234 / 135. Positives per label-year: train 2-53, eval 6-57, holdout 26-92; every label-year of every window carries both classes. For comparison, the parked annual origin-grain derivative (unicef-sdmx-refugee-origin-growth) carried only 34 positive origin-years in eval.
measurements.censoring_measured_2026_10_23: Host-year activity: 67 hosts report in 2000 growing to ~110 in recent years; among 7,622 eligible corridor-years, 7,589 (99.57%) have an active host in D+1 (missing corridor row = observed zero) and 33 (0.43%) have a host reporting nothing at all in D+1 (unobserved target; excluded). Absence of a row is treated as zero applications only when the host is still reporting.
measurements.reporting_model_mix_2026_10_23: Two reporting models inside the G/P stream: split-type codes (N/R/A/J/...) vs unsplit 'V' rows. Measured on eligible corridor-years: train window 1,238 V-model / 2,439 split-model; eval 1,918/0 V-model; holdout 1,994/0 V-model. The eval and holdout windows are 100% split-model; V-model ambiguity therefore touches only training-era rows, and the sum-all rule is cross-checked against BAMF in exactly that era. Type coexistence measured: V never coexists with N/R/A in the same corridor-year (0 of 73,051), so V is an unsplit total, not an additive category; N-with-NR/RA/SP coexistence is rare (646 cells differ between sum-all and a V/NR-preferring rule; 196 eligible).

The 2026-08-20 applications resource carries complete data through 2025, so year-D data is machine-observable at latest ~August of D+1; the conservative instant is the first observed mid-year-or-later refresh carrying year D.

review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-10-23 on written evidence: (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - publisher's own instruments (HDX package record CC BY 3.0 IGO with grant and Section 4 quoted; RDF methodology CC BY 4.0), class A, conditions carried to LICENSE.md. (2) Timing SUPPORTED with documented current-vintage assumption - annual instant = first refresh carrying year-D data (observed cadence; 2026-08-20 file carries data through 2025); the task is an explicitly-labelled publication-lag NOWCAST (abs-visitor-arrivals-direction precedent): the target value is unpublished and unavailable on the channel at the instant, while the target year itself has partially elapsed - no 'window follows the instant' claim is made; the archive is revised in place, so values are construction-time vintage, sha256-pinned, the same accepted posture as abs-visitor-arrivals-direction; a future standing vintage collector is NOT needed for the annual task but would strengthen the as-of claim if ever added. (3) Target SUPPORTED - label from the same source column at D+1, excluded from features; observed absence (missing row, active host) = 0; host-silent rows (0.43%) excluded as censored. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED - disjoint windows with both classes in every label-year, counts and clustered (origin, label-year) counts computed from the source. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - no ML-ready corridor-grain UNHCR benchmark with fixed temporal splits and a scored contract found; prior art is origin-level or EU-bilateral monthly forecasting papers and raw-panel repackages. LIMITATION recorded: the machine-fetchable extract is annual; the RDF's monthly grain stays browser-only behind the WAF, so no monthly variant is buildable from this path. The old park reason (no machine-fetchable bulk path) is resolved by the HDX global package; the correction of the 2026-10-20 search miss is recorded in both sources[1].access and measurements.
